## I. Letter to Shareholders

Looking back, 2022 was a challenging year for the tourism industry . Fortunately , in mid-October, the fourth quarter of 2022, the opening of the country's gates and the arrival of the spring swallows unblocked the moment.  Lion  Travel  gradually  recovered  from  the  epidemic,  with  revenue  in  the  fourth  quarter  of  2022 reaching more than 20 percent of revenue in the fourth quarter of 2019. However, in the face of future general economic uncertainty and the changing post-epidemic travel landscape, the Company is actively looking to the future and continuing its transformation efforts. Our vision is to build an international, digital, and capitalized lifestyle industry group.

## 1. Operating results for the previous year

## (1) Operating Report

The  Company's  consolidated  net  revenue  for  FY2022  reached  NT$3.3  billion,  and  its consolidated net loss for FY2022 was NT$730 million after tax. In the fourth quarter of 2022, outbound group travel revenue will be restored with the opening of the country's borders in October. Meanwhile, the post-epidemic era has seen a shift in travel patterns toward small-group independent travel. Lion Travel is also responding positively to this trend.  In the fourth quarter of 2022, outbound travel has resumed more than 60% of its pre-epidemic revenue performance. Besides actively resuming outbound travel, Lion Travel continues to develop T aiwan. For domestic tourism, we have deepened our efforts in railway tourism, focusing on the trend of low-carbon tourism. In FY2022, both domestic rail group tours and domestic individual travel are growing steadily .

Apart from consolidating the company's business model, Lion Travel is actively transforming to meet the rapidly changing trends in the travel industry . By utilizing digital technology , Lion Travel will expand  its  ecosystem  by  integrating  online  with  offline  physical  locations  to  increase  synergy  and optimize  the  customer  experience.  Lion  Travel  purchased  $205,380  thousand  in  special  shares  of Traveler Co., Ltd., $25,200 thousand in ordinary shares of Lavender Cottage Co., Ltd. and $15,000 thousand in Riversoft Inc. from January 1, 2022 to September 30, 2022. These investments are in line with the Company's vision and direction to build an international lifestyle group.

Traveler Co., Ltd. (branded as AsiaY o) is a platform to attract young domestic and foreign tourists and create room booking transactions, and cooperates with Lion Travel on a B&amp;B project. Lavender Cottage has created a cultural and creative entity and customized accommodation. W e create additional experiences  for  Lion's  customers,  including  long-established  corporate  clients.  Riversoft  Inc.  uses information tools to quickly assist in the implementation of the operating model of each of our branches.

## (2) Financial Reports

1. Net Assets and Liabilities:

Although the parent company, Lion Travel, has been able to conduct outbound business since October 13, 2022, the net worth of Lion Travel is still lower than that of 2021 due to the impact of the epidemic in the first three quarters of 2022, which resulted in a loss of $680 million for the year as a whole.

## 2. Profit or loss:

In  fiscal  year  2022,  financial  assets  at  fair  value  through  other  comprehensive  income  or  loss totaled NT$245,580 thousand (Traveler Co., Ltd. NT$205,380 thousand, Lavender Cottage Co., Ltd. NT$25,200  thousand,  and  Riversoft  Inc.  NT$15,000  thousand),  and  no  investment  assets  were disposed of. Lion Express $2,940 thouand, Ansett $96 thousand, and Xinflight Travel $1,871 thousand. The rest of the subsidiaries were still affected by the epidemic and had a net loss after tax.

## 2. Outline of 2023 Business Plan and Future Development Strategy

Given  the  impact  of  the  post-epidemic  tourism  recovery  in  2023  and  the  uncertainty  of  the general  economy,  Lion  Travel's  four  major  development  strategies  for  2023  include:  continued cultivation  in  T aiwan,  international  expansion,  building  capitalization  links,  enhancing  customer experience through digital technology , and creating new traffic portals. The Company will continue to expand  its  international  presence  based  on  digital  technology ,  and  provide  a  wide  range  of  travel experiences through an effective capital link. The first Lion Travel Incubator has assembled 45 teams of outstanding innovation teams in the field of niche and in-depth experience, and will help accelerate the development of future generations of travel start-up teams with our professional tourism know-how, information, technology , and capital resources.

After the information security incident at the end of 2022, the information unit will implement short-,  medium-,  and  long-term  reinforcement  programs,  including  password  reset,  comprehensive deployment protection, and database connection inventory , etc. In 2023, the Company plans to improve the information security management system and strengthen information security personnel training, exercises,  and  certification  compliance.  In  addition,  in  order  to  enhance  internationalization  and multilingual support, we plan to reorganize the schedule of multilingual and multi-currency IT systems and front-end development projects, including the development sequence of webmaster platform output, reservation products, and ticketing product processes. The first phase of the project will be completed by June 2023, with the goal of completing the webmaster platform home page, hotel page, marketing page, and  booking  and  ticketing  product  flow  page.  For  the  second  phase,  we  are  planning  for  static  + dynamic data, and dynamic data will be provided by marketing and suppliers.

## 3. Influenced by the external competitive environment

## (1) Global International Market

According to a report released by the International Air Transport Association (IA T A), by 2022, the number of passengers will reach 83% of the pandemic level and it is expected that the world as a whole will return to normal life in 2024. In fact, financial data from listed companies in the global travel industry suggest that 2022 will indeed be "the year of travel recovery". Meanwhile, visa processing provider  VFS  Global,  for  example,  said  that  visa  applications  from  January  to  May  of  this  year increased by more than 100% compared to the same period last year. With the opening of international borders, the relaxation of travel restrictions and the resumption of scheduled international flights, global travelers are "traveling with a vengeance'.

According  to  the  United  Nations  W orld  T ourism  Organization  (UNWTO)  forward-looking scenario  forecast  for  2023,  global  international  traveler  arrivals  will  reach  80  to  95  percent  of pre-Newcastle outbreak levels this year, following a better-than-expected recovery in tourism in 2022. The recovery of tourism around the world will depend on a number of factors, such as the extent of the economic slowdown, the continued recovery of travel in the Asia-Pacific region, and the evolution of the Russia-Ukraine conflict. The new year brings more reasons for optimism for the global tourism industry , with China as the world's largest outbound travel market in 2019. The recent lifting of travel restrictions related to the new epidemic and the imminent return of Chinese tourists could provide a major boost to the recovery of tourism in the Asia-Pacific region and globally .

As Euromonitor International (a global benchmark market research firm) highlights in its report "Top 10 Global Consumer Trends 2023", 10 key trends, such as human automation of human and machine experiences, more cost-efficient and effective budgeting and digital management, mass gaming, and the rise of ecology and the female economy , For those who want to live in the present and seek to get their lives back on track, they need to adjust their special products, innovate and diversify their marketing, and actively explore the overseas tourist market in order to seize the opportunity . Focusing on marketing methods with authenticity and social impact to cause resonance with the Z-generation is more important for the Taiwan market.

## (2) Taiwan Market

With the development of Internet technology , the online travel booking market has gradually become mainstream.    Among them, flight and accommodation booking is the main market. In addition, the price of air tickets and the quality of hotel accommodation become the main factors for consumers to consider,  while  young  people  are  more  willing  to  purchase  refined  and  culturally  valuable  travel experience content.

In conclusion, Taiwan's tourism market has shown a stable recovery trend. Since the opening of the  country's  borders  on  October  13,  2022,  the  fourth  quarter  of  2022,  according  to  the  statistical database of the T ourism Bureau of the Ministry of Transportation and Communications, the number of nationals going abroad reached 842,227 in the fourth quarter, compared to 74,975 in the fourth quarter of 2021, which is indeed a significant recovery . As for the number of visitors to T aiwan, the number reached 568,443 in the fourth quarter, compared to 37,560 in the fourth quarter of 2021, as Taiwan benefited from the increased international exposure during the epidemic.

## 4. Impact of future general economic uncertainty

In the next two years, the economic and political environment is expected to continue to face uncertainties  and  challenges.  Economic  growth  may  slow  down,  the  risk  of  trade  wars  and  trade protectionism may increase, and unpredictable events such as geopolitical risks and natural disasters may occur.

In response to these risks, the following measures will be taken:

- (1)  To  strengthen  the  company's  digital  innovation  capability  and  competitiveness,  plan technology  research  and  development strategy ,  and  improve  product  quality  and  service level to cope with competition and market changes.

- (2)  Monitor  changes  in  the  global  economic  and  political  environment,  and  conduct  a  risk assessment and response plans for events that may affect our business.
- (3) Maintain a sound financial position to respond to uncertainties and challenges.
- (4)  Strengthen  communication  and  coordination  with  suppliers  and  customers  to  ensure  the stability of the supply chain and customer relationships.

## 5. Conclusion

Moving forward, Lion Travel will move in the direction of internationalization, digitization, and capitalization to create more value for our shareholders. Regarding internationalization, we will continue to further promote our international presence, open up more overseas markets, and improve product quality  and  service  standards.  For  digitalization,  we  will  achieve  higher  efficiency  and  profitability through technological innovation, optimize customer experience, and realize more efficient operations. With respect to capitalization, we will promote capital operation, expand the layout of the industry chain to promote business growth, and set up a tourism industry venture capital fund to invest in tourism technology, promote industry upgrades, and shape the travel innovation ecosystem.

Thank you again for your support and trust in Lion Travel.

Lion Travel Service Co., Ltd. Chairman: Wang, Wen-Jeh

## 5. Board of Directors Diversification and Independence

## (1) Board of Directors Diversification

The Company advocates and respects the policy of diversification of directors. T o strengthen corporate governance and promote the sound development of the composition and structure of the board of directors, it is believed that the policy of diversification can help improve the overall performance of the Company . The selection and appointment of members of the board of directors is based on the principle of meritocracy . They have diverse complementary capabilities across industries, including basic composition (such as: age, gender, nationality , etc.), and they also have industrial experience and related skills (such as: aviation, shipping, Hotels, accounting, legal insurance, information technology and public welfare undertakings, etc.), as well as business judgment, business management, leadership, decision-making, and crisis management capabilities. To strengthen the functions of the board of directors and achieve the ideal goal of corporate governance, Article 20 of the Company's 'Corporate Governance Code' clearly states that the board of directors should have the following capabilities:

1. Business judgment ability 2. Accounting and financial analysis ability 3. Operation management ability 4. Crisis handling ability 5. Industry knowledge

6. International market outlook 7. Leadership ability 8. Decision-making ability

The Company's current board of directors has 6 directors (including 3 independent directors), and the overall compliance with the 'Corporate Governance Code' Article 20 specifies the capabilities that the board of directors should have, and has industry experience and professional capabilities; among them, they have rich experience in the tourism industry , Chairman W ang, W en-Jeh, Director Huang, Hsin-Chuan, and Director Lee, Chia-Yin have operational judgment, industry knowledge, leadership and decision-making capabilities; independent directors Chen, Sun-Te, Jan, Hung-Tze, and Y u, Chang-Sung have accounting and financial analysis capabilities, business management capabilities, international market views, IT or teaching. The members of the Company's board of directors are managers from the industry . Professionals with financial, business, and accounting professional backgrounds can effectively assume the duties of members of the board of directors in different fields and work backgrounds. Corporate governance and strengthening management, supervising, and evaluating the implementation of policies and operating plans at the management level, and being responsible for the overall operating conditions of the Company in terms of economy , society , and environment, and improving corporate governance and management from the perspective of stakeholders Corporation value.

## (2) Independence of the board of directors

The Company's independent directors account for 42.85% of the Board of Directors, indicating that the Board of Directors is highly independent and that there is no spousal or second degree of kinship relationships among the directors. The age distribution of the directors of the Company includes one director aged 71-80, and one directors and three independent directors aged 61-70, and one director aged 51-60. In addition to the above, the Company will strive to increase the proportion of female directors in the future. The orientation, complementarity, and implementation of director diversity have included the standards stated in Article 20 of the ' Corporate Governance Code'; in the future, the diversity policy will be updated in a timely manner depending on the operation, operation model, and development needs of the board of directors, including but not limited to basic conditions and value, professional knowledge and skills, to ensure that members of the board of directors should generally have the knowledge and skills necessary to perform their duties.

Up to now, all independent directors have complied with the Financial Supervisory Commission's regulations on independent directors, and there is no incident between the directors and independent directors in Items 3 and 4 of Article 26-3 of the Securities and Exchange Act.

2. The policy , criteria and composition of remuneration payments, the procedures for setting remuneration and its relevance to operational performance and future risk.
- A.    Directors and Supervisors

The remuneration of the Directors and the Supervisors consists of compensation, sales execution fees and remuneration for the distribution of earnings. The remuneration of the Director and the Supervisor shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of the Articles of Association, which authorize the Board of Directors to determine the level of responsibility , basic weight of appointment, acting as a joint endorsement guarantor and contribution to the Company, and the level of involvement in operations agreed by the Company , The remuneration for distribution of earnings shall be specified in the Articles of  Association.

## B.   General Manager and Deputy General Manager

The remuneration of General Manager and Deputy General Manager shall include salary , severance pay , bonuses and allowances, and employee bonuses, and shall be determined in accordance with the position held, the level of responsibility assumed, and the level of contribution made to the Company .

- C.    Relationship to operating performance and future risks.

In accordance with Article 29 of the Company's Articles of Incorporation, the Company shall set aside not less than 3% of the Company's annual profits as employee remuneration, which shall be distributed in shares or in cash as determined by the Board of Directors, and shall be paid to employees of the Company's subsidiaries who meet certain criteria. The Board of Directors may determine that not more than 2% of the total amount of the above-mentioned profits shall be allocated to the remuneration of the Director. The Company's "Annual Performance Management" is used as the basis for the review of the remuneration  process,  and  is  based  on  the  Company's  overall  operating  performance,  future  business  risks  and  development  trends,  as  well  as  the individual's  performance  achievement  rate  and  contribution  to  the  Company's  performance.  The  performance  appraisal  and  the  reasonability  of  the remuneration are reviewed by the Compensation Committee and the Board of Directors, and the remuneration system is reviewed from time to time based on actual operating conditions and relevant laws and regulations to strike a balance between sustainable operation and risk management.

## 7. Other important information to help understand the implementation of sustainable development:

## (1) Environmental protection:

- (1) The Company is concerned about the impact of environmental changes. In addition to turning off the lights during lunchtime and setting the indoor air-conditioning temperature at 24.C ~ 27.C on weekdays, the Company uses energy effectively to reduce environmental carbon emissions.

- In the meantime, we are actively promoting the use of electronics to reduce the use of paper, and continue to implement waste separation and reduction to effectively use energy. In addition, we have set up the Happy Farm Club on the top floor of the company to carry out environmental greening, so that we can achieve the goal of energy-saving and carbon reduction through effective cooling.

- (2)  Lion  Express  implemented  a  medium-sized  bus  replacement  program  from  2022  onward  to  upgrade  medium-sized  buses  to  TOYOTA  COASTER  Phase  VI  environmentally  friendly  vehicles equipped with exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) and new generation diesel particulate active filtering (DPR) systems to effectively reduce engine emissions and black smoke pollution, making travel more sustainable and friendly to the environment.    In line with the Group's active promotion of low-carbon tourism by rail, the vehicles are deployed to all areas of Taiwan to encourage tourists to take the railroad to their destinations and transfer to the Group's owned coaches to reduce the carbon emissions generated by the public's self-driving trips.

- (3) Lion Travel has incorporated Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles into its corporate decisions and is working with its supplier partners to continue promoting carbon reduction in travel, including arranging for low-carbon public transportation such as trains, bicycles, and bringing their own toiletries.    To further implement carbon and plastic reduction actions, and in response to World Earth Day, we promote the reduction of disposable goods, no longer provide bottled water for group tours, and encourage travelers to bring their own environment-friendly chopsticks and personal cups, which is equivalent to 157 towers of Taipei 101 if we calculate the amount of bottled water that Lion guests can reduce in a year!

## (2) Social welfare:

- (1) Blood donation activities: In 2022, the Company cooperated with blood donation centers to hold three blood donation activities, inviting employees to roll up their sleeves and donate blood for public welfare. 268 people participated in the activities, and 348 bags of blood were donated.

(2) Starting in year 2022, we hold a beach clean-up event. We encourage colleagues and their friends and relatives to practice environmental protection and raise their awareness on protecting the marine environment. We also encourage our employees to play an active role in reducing plasticity and waste on our coastline.

- (3) Consumers: The Company has set up a customer section on the Company's website, including a customer suggestion box and contact information, to provide a channel for consumer complaints.

- (4) Employees: The Company has created employment opportunities, established a Learning and Education Training Center, which is dedicated to handling education and training business, conducting employee training and professional development planning, and established an Employee Welfare Committee to handle various activities such as annual spring wine and raffle, health checkups, New Year's Eve street activities, year-end Christmas Thanksgiving party, etc. In addition, an employee zone is set up on the Company's website to emphasize harmonious la- bor relations and create a happy corporate atmosphere.

## ( 5 ) Stakeholder communication channels and response methods.

- (1) The Company has set up a stakeholder area on its website, including a stakeholder area, a customer area, an employee area, and a supplier area.

- (2) Each of these areas has a channel for disclosing complaints and contact information, and information on the frequency of communication and response methods for stakeholder negotiations can also be found in the stakehold- er section of the Company's website.

## (10) Implementation Status of the Internal Control System

## 1. Internal Control System Statement

## Lion Travel Service Co. Ltd.

## Internal Control System Statement

Date: March 23, 2023

The Company declares the following with regard to its internal control system in 2022, based on the findings of a self-assessment:

1. The Company is fully aware that establishing, operating, and maintaining an internal control system are the responsibility of its Board of Directors and managerial officers. The Company has established such a system aimed at providing reasonable assurance of the achievement of objectives in the effectiveness and efficiency of operations (including profits, performance, and safeguard of asset security), reliability , timeliness, transparency , and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and bylaws.
2. An internal control system has inherent limitations. No matter how perfectly designed, an effective internal control system can provide only reasonable assurance of accomplishing the three goals mentioned above. Furthermore, the effectiveness of an internal control system may change along with changes in environment or circumstances. The internal control system of  the  Company contains self-monitoring mechanisms, however, and the Company takes corrective actions as soon as a deficiency is identified.
3.  The Company judges the design and operating effectiveness of its internal control system based on the criteria provided in the "Regulations Governing the Establishment of Internal Control Systems by Public Companies" (herein below, the 'Regulations'). The internal control system judgment criteria adopted by the Regulations divide internal control into five elements based on the process of management control: (1) Control environment, (2) Risk assessment, (3) Control activities, (4) Information and communications, and (5) Monitoring activities. Each element further contains several items. Please refer to the Regulations for details.
4. The Company has evaluated the design and operating effectiveness of its internal control system according to the aforesaid criteria.
5. Based on the findings of the assessment mentioned in the preceding paragraph, the Company believes that on December 31, 2022, its internal control system (including its supervision and management of subsidiaries), encompassing internal controls for understanding of the degree of achievement of operational effectiveness and efficiency objectives, reliability , timeliness, transparency , and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and bylaws, was effectively designed and operating, and reasonably assured the achievement of the above stated objectives.
6. This Statement will become a major part of the content of the Company's Annual Report and Prospectus, and will be made public. Any falsehood, concealment, or other illegality in the content made public will entail legal liability under Articles 20, 32, 171, and 174 of the Securities and Exchange Law.
7. This statement has been passed by the Board of Directors Meeting of the Company held on March 23, 2023, where none of the 6 attending directors, including attendance by proxy , expressed dissenting opinions and all affirmed the content of this Statement, and hereby declare.

Lion Travel Service Co., Ltd.

4.1.6 The Company's dividend policy and implementation status

1. Dividend policy stipulated in the articles of association of the Company

According to Article 30 of the Company's proposed Articles of Association, if there is a surplus in the Company's annual final accounts, taxes shall be paid in accordance with the  law,  and  after  making  up  for  the  accumulated  losses,  10%  shall  be  raised  as  the statutory surplus reserve, but when the statutory surplus reserve has reached the paid-in capital  of  the  Company,  it  may  no  longer  be  listed,  and  the  rest  shall  be  listed  or transferred to the special surplus reserve in accordance with the provisions of the decree; if there is still a surplus, and the same accumulated undistributed surplus, the Board of Directors  shall  prepare  a  surplus  distribution  bill  and  submit  it  to  the  shareholders' meeting for a resolution to distribute shareholders' dividends. The Company's dividend policy  is  in  line  with  the  current  and  future  development  plans,  considering  the investment environment, capital needs and domestic and foreign competition conditions, and taking into account the interests of shareholders and other factors, it can allocate not less  than  10%  of  the  surplus  for  distribution  every  year,  and  distribute  shareholder dividends. When distributing shareholder dividends, it can be done in cash or stocks, of which the cash dividend is not less than 30% of the total dividend.

2. Proposed dividend distribution at the shareholders' meeting

The  Company's  net  loss  for  fiscal  year  2022  was  NT$684,284,600,  and  after  adding  the remeasurement of the defined benefit plan to retained earnings, the total accumulated deficit for the period was NT$669,635,774. In accordance with Article 239 of the Company Act, capital surplus is proposed to be used to offset the loss of NT$669,635,774, and the loss to be offset after the offsetting period is NT$0. The proposal will be processed in accordance with the relevant regulations after the resolution of the shareholders' meeting on June 20, 2023.

3. Expected significant changes in dividend policy: None.

- 4.1.7 The effect of the proposed gratis allotment of shares at the shareholders' meeting on the Company's operating results and earnings per share: Not applicable.

## 4.1.8 Remuneration of employees and directors

1.  The proportion or scope of remuneration of employees and directors contained in the articles of association of the Company

In accordance with the provisions of Article 29 of the Company's proposed articles of association: If the Company makes a profit in the year, it shall allocate not less than 3% as the remuneration of employees, and the Board of Directors shall decide to distribute it  in  shares  or  cash,  and  the  distribution  target  includes  employees  of  subordinate companies who meet certain conditions; the Company can make a profit, and the Board of Directors shall decide to allocate not more than 2% as the remuneration of directors. However,  when  the  Company  still  has  accumulated  losses,  it  should  reserve  the compensation amount in advance, and then allocate the remuneration of employees and directors and supervisors in accordance with the proportion of the preceding paragraph. The term "Annual profit" as used in Item 1 refers to the pre-tax profit of the current year before  deducting  the  profit  before  the  distribution  of  employee  remuneration  and director remuneration. The  distribution of employee  remuneration  and  directors' remuneration shall be made by the Board of Directors with the attendance of more than two-thirds  of  the  directors  and  a  resolution  approved  by  a  majority  of  the  directors' present, and a report to the shareholders' meeting shall be submitted.

2.  The  basis  for  the  estimation  of  the  remuneration  of  employees  and  directors  in  the current period, the basis for the calculation of the number of shares of the remuneration of employees  distributed  by  shares, and  the accounting  treatment  if the actual distribution amount is different from the estimated number:

After the end of the year, when there is a major change in the amount of disbursement determined by the board of directors, the change shall be adjusted to the original annual expenses; at the time of the shareholders' meeting resolution, if the amount still changes, it  shall  be  processed  in  accordance  with  the  change  in  accounting  estimates,  and  the adjustment shall be recorded in the year of the shareholders' meeting resolution.

3. The Board of Directors approved the distribution of remuneration:

On March 23, 2023, the Board of Directors resolved not to distribute remuneration to employees and directors for the  year 2022 due to the lack of profits and submitted a report to the 112th Annual General Meeting of Shareholders.

4.  The  actual  distribution  of  employee  and  director's  remuneration  in  the  previous  year (including the number of shares distributed, the amount, and the price of shares) and the difference  between  the  distribution  and  the  recognition  of  employee  and  director's remuneration should be stated, the reasons for the difference, and the handling of the situation:
- (1) Distribution: On June 16, 2022, the Company resolved at the annual shareholders' meeting to not distribute employee and director's remuneration, which is the same as the proposed distribution by the original board of directors and has been implemented.
- (2) If the actual allotment differs from the recognized amount, the difference, the reasons, and the handling of the difference:

There is no difference between the amount of employees' and directors' remuneration and the amount recognized  as  proposed  by  the  board  of  directors  and  resolved  by  the  shareholders' meeting.

- 4.1.9 Repurchase of the Company's shares:

The Company has not repurchased any shares of the Company in the most recent year and as of the date of publication of this annual report.

## V. Operational Highlights

## 5.1 Business Activities

- 5.1.1 Business Scope
1. Main content of business: T ourism.
2. Business Ratio

The main services provided by the Company are arranging domestic and overseas tours and accommodations for  tourists,  handling  immigration  and  visa  procedures  on  behalf  of  tourists, selling domestic and overseas transportation tickets, and purchasing domestic and overseas tickets and checking baggage on behalf of tourists. The following table shows the proportion of operations by consumer travel destination:

Unit: NT$ thousand; %

| Year  Item  2022  Sales amount  Business Ratio  Outbound Travel  754,730  22.87  Inbound Travel  2,047,942  62.05  Others  497,594  15.08  Total  3,300,266  100.00   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|

3. Current products (services) of the Company
- (1) Accepting the commission to sell inbound and outbound sea, land, and air transportation tickets  or  purchase  domestic  and  international  tickets  and  check  baggage  on  behalf  of passengers.
- (2)  Accepting the entrustment of passengers to handle exit and entry and visa procedures.
- (3)  Receiving inbound and outbound tourists and arranging travel, accommodation, and tour guides.
- (4)  Organizing  tours  on  its  own  in  the  form  of  package  tours  and  arranging  inbound  and outbound sightseeing tours, accommodation and food, and providing related services.
- (5) Entrusting Class A travel industry to solicit business on behalf of the preceding paragraph.
- (6) Entrusting Class B travel industry to solicit inbound group travel business on behalf of Type IV .
- (7)  Acting as an agent for the foreign travel industry for liaison, promotion, quotation, etc.
- (8) Other matters related to inbound and outbound travel as approved by the central competent authority .
4. New products (services) to be developed

With the growing experience and maturity of the travel market, tourists are no longer satisfied with the products or services offered by traditional operators. In the past, the travel industry was unilaterally dominated by the travel industry , but now travelers want more diversified services and more differentiated travel products. As a result, the Company , which has been in the travel business for many years, gradually develops the following innovative new products and services to meet the latest trends and topics in the market and to ensure our position as a leading brand in the market.

- (1) Theme-based travel for segmented groups.
- (2) In-depth travel, local experience.
- (3) Medical conventions and incentive travel.
- (4) Contracted tours and customer orientation.
- (5) Mobile tools, real-time services.
- (6) Virtual and reality channels, combined with the split.
- (7) Network relationship, academic operation.

## 5.1.2 Industry Overview

1. Current status and development of the industry

The Company is in the travel industry, and its main operations are selling or purchasing tickets for domestic and international  tourism businesses on behalf of the Company, receiving domestic and foreign tourists, arranging tours, accommodations,  guided  tours,  and  combining  various  tourism  products,  and organizing tours for domestic and foreign tourists, and receiving service revenues such as handling fees or commissions. The travel industry acts as an intermediary between  tourists  and  tourism  enterprises  such  as  hotels,  airlines,  and  leisure businesses, and is an inseparable part of the tourism industry.

In  March  2020,  the  World  Health  Organization  (WHO)  declared  a  global pandemic  of  novel  coronavirus  pneumonia  (COVID-19),  constituting  a  "public health  emergency  of  international  concern"  (PHEIC).  As  a  result,  the  tourism business in many places has dropped sharply. The Tourism Bureau of the Ministry of  Transportation  and  Communications  (MOTC)  issued  a  letter  to  all  travel agencies,  banning  tours  and  overseas  tours  from  March  19,  2020.  In  order  to prevent  the  outbreak,  the  MOTC  continues  to  suspend  the  travel  industry  from organizing tours to foreign countries and receiving inbound tour groups to Taiwan. In early 2021, the international tourism market was again affected by the outbreak of  the  COVID-19  virus  variant,  and  countries  raised  travel  restrictions  and increased the number of destinations with completely closed borders, and measures such as mandatory quarantine continued to interfere with the progress of tourism recovery.  Subsequent outbreaks of COVID-19 cluster infections in China have led to the extension of border control measures, suspending the entry of non-nationals without a R.O.C. residence permit, and the declaration of a Level 3 alert in May after  the  rapid  deterioration  of  the  COVID-19  epidemic  in  China,  which  has severely  impacted  the  local  travel  and  accommodation  industry.  In  view  of  the rising  global  COVID-19  epidemic  and  the  continued  spread  of  the  Delta  and Omicron  variants,  strict  border  control  measures  continue  to  be  implemented  to prevent the influx of cases from abroad from increasing the burden on quarantine and prevention capacity and medical resources.

In  view  of  the  full  impact  of  the  epidemic  on  the  global  airline  and  hotel industries, and the fact that the development of the epidemic is not  yet clear, the Company continues to strengthen the cultivation of talents and initiate a strategic organizational  restructuring  plan  to  integrate  the  staff  into  the  international  travel market, and We  are also working with the government to strengthen the government's relief and  revitalization  programs  and are working with central and local  government  agencies  to  secure  domestic  tourism-related  bids.  In  order  to overcome the downturn in the industry, we waited for the unblocking of our borders and the relaunch of outbound tourism.

After nearly three years of blockage, the second half of 2022 has seen a gradual easing of travel policies around the world as vaccination coverage rates continue to increase  and  the  rate  of  severe  new  cases  of  pneumonia  decreases.  The  earliest relaxation was in Europe and the United States and Canada. In Asia, Japan, Korea, and  Southeast  Asia  are  gradually  relaxing  their  border  control  policies.  Taiwan finally  opened  its  doors  on  October  13,  2022,  with  the  revised  policy  of  "0  +  7" border control on return to Taiwan and no quarantine upon entry, which requires only  seven  days  of  independent  management.  The  previous  restrictions  on  the number of arrivals and home quarantine measures were gradually lifted. Taiwan's outbound and inbound tourism officially resumes normal operations.

To precisely market the domestic and international target markets, it is necessary to stimulate the boom of international tourism, and accelerate the recovery and growth opportunities of the international tourism market to Taiwan.

In response to the post-epidemic market and to promote tourism development, the government has re-adjusted the strategic layout to "continuously boost domestic tourism first, and then set up an international tourism plan", and has developed 5 strategies,  10  key  points,  and  24  implementation  measures,  supplemented  by  the restructuring of the Tourism Bureau and increased investment in resources, in the hope  that  resources  can  be  optimized  and  a  deep,  diversified,  and  high-quality tourism environment can be established. Promote the short-term "Tourism Industry Relief Program" and the medium-term "Tourism Industry Recovery and Revitalization Program" and "Tourism Upgrade and Foresight Program" to revitalize  the  industry  and  boost  the  tourism  market.  The  competent  authorities have launched the Tourism Industry Relief Program to help stabilize employment and  mitigate  the  impact  of  the  epidemic  on  the  tourism  industry.  The  authorities have also planned the revitalization and recovery of "domestic tourism" through a three-stage travel plan of epidemic prevention and travel, peace of mind travel, and international  tourism,  as  well  as  the  relaxation  of  various  epidemic  prevention measures,  so  that  the  people  of  Taiwan  can  share  the  wonderful  results  of  the success  of  epidemic  prevention  and  gradually  revitalize  the  domestic  tourism market.

In  the  past  two  years,  Taiwan  has  become  a  relatively  safe  travel  destination compared  to  other  countries  in  the  world.  In  order  to  grab  this  opportunity  of industry  transformation  and  to  maintain  the  temperature  of  the  inbound  travel market, the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC) has launched the Year of Bicycle Tourism 2021 and the Year of Railway Tourism 2022 to provide environmental preparation, tour linkage, special activities, and diversified marketing. It also encourages the industry to develop thematic tourism products to sustain  the  vitality  of  the  domestic  tourism  market,  hoping  that  the  industry  as  a whole can turn the crisis into an opportunity to transform Taiwan from a country of epidemic  prevention  into  a  country  of  tourism.  Therefore,  with  the  government's continued promotion of relevant policies, the number of national tourism arrivals in Taiwan will be boosted and is expected to maintain its growth in 2022.

2. Linkages among upstream, midstream, and downstream of the industry

The tourism industry can be divided into upstream suppliers of tourism products, such as airlines,  hotels,  restaurants,  car  rental  companies,  and  train  transportation.  Midstream  travel agencies (including integrated travel agencies and A and B travel agencies). In the downstream, there are the consumers or tourists.

The  travel  industry  occupies  a  midstream  position  in  the  tourism  industry ,  acting  as  an intermediary between tourism companies and tourists. The industry acts as an agent for upstream tourism  resources  such  as  the  airline  industry ,  transportation  industry ,  catering  industry ,  and lodging industry , and is also entrusted by downstream travelers to purchase tickets from domestic and foreign tourism companies, or to organize tours on its own in the form of package tours, integrate  upstream  tourism  resources  and  design  and  package  tourism  products,  and  provide tourism services to downstream travelers. ## 3. Product (Service) Development Trend

Over the years, Taiwan's tourism industry has been developed on the basis of a diversified and open global layout. It has been more than 40 years since Taiwan opened to foreign tourism in 1979. In 2008, Taiwan's tourism industry was further opened up to tourists from China. In the past few years, Taiwan's tourism industry has been greatly enhanced and changed in both volume and value,  which  has  had  a  profound  impact  on  T aiwan's  economic  growth  and  political  and economic society . For more than 40 years, the domestic tourism industry has been accumulating travel experience and the world has evolved into the concept of a global village. The rise of selfguided travel, more in-depth themed tours, and high-end travel at the top of the pyramid will be the main trends in the future travel market and the main business on which the travel industry will depend.   In  terms  of  tourism  destinations,  due  to  global  climate  change  and  political  factors, natural disasters, and unrest around the world, many tourist attractions are often temporarily or permanently closed due to irresistible factors, so that the development of scenic spots will not be affected by the closure of a single scenic spot.  In terms of traveler services, in addition to the traditional  itinerary  quotation,  many  channel  operators  are  more  committed  to  better  quality services,  more  convenient  procurement  and  booking  process,  and  one-stop  shopping  website content, providing a complete and value-added product content to provide a value-added and differentiated travel itinerary . In addition, more forward-looking industry players have proposed

innovative travel itineraries, constantly developing new attractions, new ways to play , and diverse and variable product content to enrich and meet customer needs.

The impact of the global pandemic of the novel coronavirus pneumonia (COVID-19), as well as international instability , and global climate change, have created the potential for unanticipated natural and man-made disasters in all regions of the world. The travel industry can only provide diversified travel products without the influence of a single region. In response to the impact of the epidemic on the global tourism industry , the Company has made every effort to maintain corporate  momentum  in  the  face  of  operational  pressure.  The  Group  has  made  rapid organizational  adjustments  and  staffing  changes  to  transform  its  operations  and  expand  its domestic tourism market share with the goal of deepening cooperation opportunities with central government, local,  and  private  DMU  organizations  and  pan-tourists.  Due  to  the  unavoidable decline  in  revenue  due  to  the  new  COVID-19  epidemic,  the  Group  has  been  actively  and continuously controlling  expenses and costs internally  and has launched a travel e-commerce layout with the goal of enhancing the use of information technology and intelligence. In addition, the  Group has been working with the  government's  bid operation strategy to obtain superior crowds and cost advantages, such as large Taiwan Railway or high-speed rail stations and ports, to adjust the manpower for physical channel operation including Hualien, Nangang, New WuRi, New Zuoying, Fangliao service reception (reception) and VIP lounge of the integrated use, both field operation efficiency and market service function.

The  company  also  strengthens  the  extension  of  the  core  competitive  items  of  domestic tourism.  For  example,  we  will  strengthen  our  own  Lion  Express  operation  capability  for transportation. T o enhance the number and quality of buses, coaches, minibuses, and tour guides. Continue  to  strengthen  the  depth  and  breadth  of  the  Group's  four  inbound  travel  operating segments, including "Rail" - railway , "Road" - road transportation, "Forest" - forest resources, and "Harbor" - water and sea transportation, and continue to strengthen the Group's mastery of market components and resources. We will continue to enhance the depth of our market component resources.

## 4. Competition

In addition to the government's policy of promoting the tourism industry , the development of Taiwan's travel industry has been changing from a competitive model of the number of tours to a competitive model of tailor-made services for consumers, with the influx of foreign tourists and the rise of nationals' self-help travel.  How to target specific groups and plan travel itineraries that best meet consumers' needs in order to build the company's brand image is an important survival key for travel industry players. For the tourism industry , people flow means cash flow.

The outbreak of the COVID-19 epidemic has led to a significant drop in overseas travelers, bringing  a  wave  of  winter  to  T aiwan's  tourism  industry .  In  the  "post-epidemic"  era,  the  next challenge for travel industry operators is whether they can recover quickly .

## 5.1.3 T echnology and R&amp;D Overview

## 1. Level of technology in the business

The Company has set up a dedicated management planning team and a product innovation center to innovate  itineraries,  optimize  processes,  and  improve  mechanisms.  Through  the  Product  Innovation Center,  we  hope  to  transform  the  tourism  industry  from  basic  research  to  application  development. Through the Product Innovation Center, we will expand our core technology capabilities, innovate our product mix, and develop e-commerce technologies and high-niche tourism products that meet market needs in the following steps.

## (1) Market Research

Through seasonal product innovation competitions, we introduce innovative methodologies and incorporate value-added elements of the experience economy . Our team members are experienced and professional product designers in the industry , and are able to develop products with high market

acceptance based on seasonality , flight utilization, attraction planning, and cost control.    However, the travel market is changing rapidly . In addition, to be able to develop highly competitive products in the long run, we need specialists to understand market trends based on traveler demand, competitive analysis,  product  lifecycle,  marketing,  and  customer  crowding,  etc.  Then,  through  professional teamwork, we can continuously develop market-leading products and technologies to become the benchmark of the tourism industry .

- (2) Data Analysis

In recent years, the use of big data has taken on a significant role in the service industry . W e have set  up  a  data  decision-making  department  to  collect  and  chart  a  large  amount  of  information  on operations,  marketing,  consumer  behavior,  and  event  management,  and  apply  it  to  all  products, channels, and marketing meetings as a reference for supervisors to make decisions. The experience of handling the epidemic has also been internalized and documented by the organization. In recent years, Lion  Travel  has  also  been  actively  using  big  data  analysis  to  manage  customer  relationship management (CRM) and to analyze and make decisions based on marketing activities.

- (3) T echnology Development

Currently ,  our  product  development  team  plans  to  integrate  ERP  (Enterprise  Performance Management) with CRM, SCM (supplier chain management), and KM (Knowledge management) in order to continue to create industry-leading IT technologies and service flows, and to continuously enhance  hardware  improvements  and  software  optimizations.  Our  goal  is  to  integrate  upstream, midstream, and downstream supply and service chains to become the most efficient travel company in the tourism industry .

- (4) Product Design

To assist the product department in developing various types and levels of products that are more sophisticated and meet the needs of our customers than those of other companies in the industry; this is done through the analysis of target groups and market positioning, so that all visitors can have a wonderful travel experience during their trip with us.

- (5) Process Optimization

To improve the performance of our operations and to meet the changing needs and expectations of  our  employees  and  external  customers,  we  are  continuously  improving  and  optimizing  our processes. Through process reengineering and innovation, the quality assurance department and the management planning team are striving for breakthroughs through proposals for improvement, so that the company's internal and external services and quality can meet the expectations of employees and customers.

2. Research and Development Overview: Our company is in the tourism service industry and does not have a full-time R&amp;D department.

## 5.1.4 Long-term and short-term business development plans

1. Short-term business development plan

In the post-epidemic era, facing the recovery of outbound travel after three years of the epidemic, the Company's near-term business development plans are as follows:

- (1) Continue to develop diversified products for creative travel and maintain our position as a leading brand in the market

The world's travel industry is changing rapidly , and as travelers' experience abroad increases and the travel  market  becomes  more  mature,  the  one-way  tourism  products  and  services  offered  by  the traditional  travel  industry  can  no  longer  meet  the  changing  needs  of  consumers.  Therefore,  the Company will gradually develop creative tourism products and services in line with the market trend. For example, through different targeted groups, we will launch thematic tours and customized tours to ensure Lion Travel's position as a leading brand in the market.

- (2) Extend core competencies and utilize mobile tools

In  recent  years,  the  search  for  travel  information  and  products  has  shifted  from  print  media  to

electronic networks, and further to mobile commerce. "Technology , creativity , and knowledge" are the  three  core  competencies  that  we  have  accumulated  and  deepened  over  time  and  applied  to support  innovative  business  models,  integrate  global  travel  resources,  and  optimize  consumer experience under the guidance of the Group's strategy . Under the impact of the epidemic in the past, the Company has reduced the number of physical stores and restructured overseas offices to reduce rental expenses. At the same time, we have strengthened the use of digital tools, such as APP , LINE, and other information and communication tools, enhanced CRM and various members' operations, optimized UI and UX experience development, and focused our resources on optimizing online user service experience.

The company has demonstrated the value-added services of "The Future Begins" and Breezy Blue in the mobile field. The company has worked with designers to create Taiwan Railway waiting rooms and more fixed-site aesthetic commercial spaces (Sunongshan Cultural and Creative Park.), and to create a beautiful space and service experience. The management planning team and the government project team are working together to interpret government policies and write project proposals. In addition to acquiring the right to operate Taiwan Railway's tourist and aesthetic trains and  venues,  we  will  continue  to  expand  our  government  project  performance  with  the  Group's strengths.

- (3) Differentiation of Inbound travel Products to Achieve Competitive Advantages In recent years, the Company has started to operate large and rare domestic transportation, from chartering international cruise ships to packaging them as round-the-island and island-hopping trips, which  caused  a  great  impact  in  the  early  stage  of  the  domestic  epidemic.  In  terms  of  railroad operation, we started to obtain major bids from the Railroad Bureau such as "The Future Begins", "Breezy Blue", and "The Kitchen" at the end of 2020, and at the same time, we obtained the Alishan Forest Railway charter from the Forestry Bureau. The company has also laid the foundation for its future role as an integral part of T aiwan's railway tourism. The high selling price and high gross profit of the rail-themed tours have also enabled the Company to slightly alleviate the losses incurred during the epidemic. The Company will continue to develop inbound travel product differentiation and promote superior products to deepen the competitiveness of inbound travel.
2. Long-term business development plan
- (1) Continue to expand and integrate virtual and real channels to create multiple profit models The Company has created the largest travel website in Taiwan through online operations. Through the  development  of  various  technologies,  the  company  has  been  able  to  deliver  information  to consumers and place orders regardless of time and geographical restrictions. However, in today's consumer environment, customers are less loyal to brands, more price-sensitive, and more consumer conscious, so it is not possible to sell through only one channel. Therefore, through the development of  store  locations,  we  can  provide  customers  with  more  detailed  services,  provide  them  with sufficient travel information through face-to-face services, determine their attitudes and true thoughts, and then decide how to recommend products or convince them. With the trend of chain, large-scale, and information, the development of store services has evolved from single-store operation to multistore  operation.  Through  the  management  of  local  customer  base  in  stores,  we  can  "grasp customers", "analyze customers", and "understand customers", and pay attention to the development of "potential customers", so we can integrate the network and store channels in parallel, splitting and combining to create the maximum channel energy and profit.
- (2) From "source thinking" to "destination management", we are able to achieve one-stop operation efficiency

As the Company operates in the travel market for many years, it has huge inbound travel consumer resources and can establish close and good business relationships with upstream suppliers and has better bargaining power compared to its peers. In addition, we have set up overseas subsidiaries in the United States, Canada, Hong Kong, New Zealand, Australia, Thailand, and Japan to integrate local travel quality and resources and to provide local services.

- (3) Continue to introduce e-commerce operation mechanism to extend core competitiveness

"Technology,  creativity ,  and  knowledge"  are  the  three  core  competencies  that  Lion  Group  has accumulated and deepened over a long period of time and applied to support innovative operation models, integrate global tourism resources, and optimize consumer experience under the guidance of the Group's strategy .

The stock and flow of travel knowledge and experience has not only shortened the learning curve and reduced the cost of trial and error for Lion. Based on our past experience in rapid response and rich processing, Lion Travel has further established the "Data Decision Department" to data and chart a large amount of information on operations, marketing, marketing, consumer behavior, and event handling, and apply it to all products, channels, and marketing meetings as a reference for executive decision making.

- (4) Increasing relationships and improving academic management

Our company actively strengthens relationships with all sectors, cultivates good contacts, and seeks opportunities for business or tourism cooperation. In addition, we have strengthened our interaction with  the  academic  community  by  cooperating  with  schools  on  educational  programs  and establishing internship travel agencies in order to develop future company talents. In addition, we have also placed emphasis on lifelong learning for our employees. Over the years, we have invested in the MA talent pool, cultivated management and planning talent, subsidized senior executives to study at EMBA schools in various locations around the world, planned overseas rotations, and other talent  cultivation  measures,  as  well  as  fostered  cross-country  and  cross-divisional  cooperation through large-scale projects, which have helped Lion Travel to expand its business. This energy is the  driving  force  behind  the  development  of  new  services,  such  as  group  tours  and  ground transportation between global locations and destination travel.

- (5) Focus on a new model of smart tourism with a Regional Hub as the core

The Company recognizes that the tourism industry will undergo a structural transformation and innovation  after  the  epidemic.  The  new  travel  model  will  be  an  experience-based,  data-based personalized service that integrates the different supply chains of trip content (media), mobile venues (transportation),  and  fixed  venues  (tickets).  Our  experienced  IT  team  developed  Mobility  as  a Service  (MaaS),  a  digital  software  for  shared  transportation,  as  the  starting  point  for  our  digital transformation. The company has used inbound travel as a framework to expand its business model to overseas travel markets in the post-epidemic era.
