After three years of the COVID-19 epidemic, border control measures have been implemented by various countries to prevent the spread of the epidemic, which has severely impacted the global

tourism industry and caused a sharp decline in the number of visitors to Taiwan and overseas trips by nationals. According to the Bureau of Tourism of the Ministry of Transportation and Communications (MOTC), the global COVID-19 epidemic has affected Taiwan's border policy since 2020 and the ban has been extended indefinitely. Although in the second half of 2021, many countries will gradually lift their home control and other blockade measures after the epidemic has subsided, economic activities will gradually resume and inbound travel policies will be encouraged to stimulate tourism-related spending. However, the epidemic has resumed in some countries after the lifting of the embargo and the international business travel market remains sluggish. Therefore, in 2021, both the number of overseas travelers and the number of visitors to Taiwan declined significantly. In 2022, as the  epidemic  eases,  countries  gradually  lift  their  border  control  measures.  In  the  post-epidemic recovery outbound tourism has become the main driving force of tourism recovery. Both the number of outbound travelers and the number of tourists coming to Taiwan have recovered significantly from the bottom.

After three years of the impact of the epidemic. In the post-epidemic era of global tourism, the tourism industry is facing the problem of transformation. The Company will continue to deepen its tourism business and integrate digital technology to develop diversified tourism products and services to maintain its leading position in the domestic tourism industry.

## 3. Future Supply and Demand and Growth of the Market

With the continuous improvement of living standards, people's demand for leisure activities has also increased significantly, and travel has become a trend. Because tourism allows people to enjoy the world's rich cultures and natural landscapes, it brings people closer together and demonstrates the common  humanity  of  human  beings.  According  to  the  2017  Tourism  Competitiveness  Report published by the World Economic Forum, the total revenue of global tourism has exceeded global GDP by more than 10%. Looking back at the decade before the epidemic, the number of people traveling abroad has been growing every year, and by 2019, the number of international travelers worldwide will have reached 1.46 billion, driving the booming development of the global tourism industry, which has become a global trend for all countries.

According to the Directorate-General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics, Executive Yuan, the annual economic growth rate for 2022 is forecasted to be 3.2%, which is slightly lower than  the annual economic growth rate of 6.45% in 2021, but the GDP per person is still up at US$35,244. . The growth in real GDP will support the leisure travel market. Household income, household disposable income, and consumption tendency are also gradually increasing, and people are more and more concerned about the improvement of quality of life, driving tourism opportunities. The rise of selfguided travel, more in-depth themed tours, and high-end travel at the top of the pyramid will be the main trends in the future tourism market.

The  World  Tourism  Organization  (UNWTO)  actively  advocates  for  sustainable  tourism, emphasizing that while tourism industries and economies are being upgraded, the overall tourism environment, economy and social and cultural development should be kept in perspective. The AsiaPacific  Economic  Cooperation  (APEC)  has  also  advocated  Inclusive  Growth  since  2010,  and  in recent years has incorporated the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), focusing on natural resource sectors, including forests, agriculture, fisheries, mining, and tourism, to promote inclusive and sustainable resource development. With the official reopening of the border on October 13,  2022,  the  epidemic  has  subsided.  The  Director  of  the  Tourism  Bureau  of  the  Ministry  of Transportation and Communications (MOTC) also said that in order to meet the United Nations Sustainable  Development  Goals  (SDGs)  and  the  National  Council  for  Sustainable  Development, Executive Yuan's " Taiwan's Sustainable Development Goals", the Bureau of Tourism has taken into account "economic growth", "social progress", and "environmental protection".  The Tourism Bureau has set the specific goal of "promoting sustainable tourism development, guiding the tourism industry to provide a green, local tourism model, creating a sustainable tourism environment in Taiwan and enhancing the value of the industry". The Tourism Bureau has also set three indicators for sustainable

tourism development, including the  "growth rate of overall tourism revenue" (economic growth), "growth rate of employment in the tourism industry" (employment growth), and "eco-tourism theme itineraries" (green economy).

The global tourism industry has been hit hard by the epidemic in the past three years, but in 2022, as the epidemic gradually eased and border control measures were lifted, post-epidemic retaliatory outbound travel has become a major driver of tourism recovery, and it is expected that the tourismrelated industries will gradually return to their pre-epidemic growth with the help of rising tourism demand and government policies.

4. Competitive niche
- (1) Integration of various operational capabilities and IT/ICT systems to provide a full range of travel products and services

At present, our company has established a comprehensive computerized system, especially through the internal network to connect the itinerary planning, supplier management, procurement components, shelf sales, and other departments of the operation process to the computer network system, fully integrated with the company's real-time information.  In addition, in order to cope with the advent of the mobile business era, the Company not only publishes travel information and product marketing catalogs on the Internet but also launches an APP, which allows consumers to conveniently  use  various  carriers  to  inquire  and  order  our  travel  products  through  the  cloud database, providing consumers with more real-time and complete travel services.

- (2) Integrated marketing of virtual and real channels between the Internet and stores to create multiple profit models

In order to meet the travel needs of consumers, our company continues to integrate online and offline services in a comprehensive channel layout, using virtual networks and physical stores to provide  consumers  with  more  time-saving,  complete,  and  professional  travel  services.    In  the virtual  network  operation,  in  order  to  serve  such  a  large  customer  demand,  the  company  has established a quality online sales and customer service center to provide 24-hour travel services, and actively develop mobile applications.  In terms of physical store operations, we have deepened the aesthetic space experience, integrated business space displays, expert meeting rooms, themed seminars, and explanatory meetings, and combined them with the "Tourmaline" series of products, which are positioned for in-depth experience, to develop a high-end market. With the opening of our borders, the international travel market has regained its vitality, and we are planning to resume our physical stores in the metropolitan areas of North, Central, and South Taiwan, as well as in other  countries  and  cities.  Unitravel  Service  Co.,  Ltd.  of  the  Group's  new  brand  "Unitravel" operates  a  large-scale  market  in  the  same  industry  and  enhances  more  detailed  services  to customers, and provides customers with adequate travel information and product services through "face-to-face" services close to the end customers.

- (3)  Integration  of  tourism  products  with  cultural  and  creative  industries,  planning  to  launch  niche market products

With the increase in income and standard of living of the Chinese people, the number of trips abroad has increased, and the traditional travel methods have gradually failed to meet the needs of travelers with special needs for a certain type of travel. With this in mind, the company is now going  to  analyze  various  target  groups  according  to  the  age,  occupation,  interest,  theme,  and behavior pattern of travelers. In addition, the Company will combine cultural and creative activities to design various niche tourism products, such as adventure, festival, sports, monuments, music, food, cruise, etc., in order to meet the needs and expectations of various traveler groups for specific types of travel.

- (4) Establishment of an internal knowledge platform organization and emphasis on talent cultivation to consolidate operational strength

Consolidate  the  company's  internal  knowledge  of  the  tourism  business,  both  explicit  and implicit, into a knowledge management database, so that the knowledge and experience related to

the  tourism  business  can  be  continuously  passed  on  and  extended.  Therefore,  we  are  actively establishing various SOP processes and building and promoting a knowledge platform through a knowledge management system that uses value activities as the core and standard duties as the weft, in order to shorten learning time and improve work efficiency and effectiveness. In addition, in order to provide better services to our expanding customer base, we have always paid attention to recruiting and cultivating talents. For example, we have a number of professional managers who have a deep understanding of the travel market and full knowledge of travel products, and cultivate management  and  planning  talents,  subsidize  senior  executives  to  study  at  EMBA  schools  in various locations around the world, and plan overseas rotations. In order to realize the global bases as  a  source  of  motivation  for  tour  formation  and  ground  transportation,  and  to  develop  new services such as travel to source and reach destinations, the company has been able to expand its business territory.

- (5) Actively develop content marketing and community management to move into the lifestyle culture and creative industry

The Company's 3C operation model integrates Content, Community, and Commerce, and continues to innovate products, channels, and marketing to enhance the diversity of travel services and  provide  the  most  suitable  travel  choices  from  corporate  customers  to  general  travelers. Integrate  from  tourism  brand  to  lifestyle  culture  and  creative  industry.  To  provide  precise  and satisfying market demand for thematic travel, thus enhancing the mindset of consumers in the travel  industry  and  creating  a  flagship  lifestyle  service  industry,  evolving  from  a  travel  service provider to a lifestyle interpreter.

## 5. Favorable and unfavorable factors of development prospect and countermeasures

(1) Favorable factors

A. The government vigorously promotes the tourism and leisure industry

The United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) has designated 2017 as the "International  Year  of  Sustainable  Tourism  Development  (IYSTD),"  which  emphasizes sustainable  development  in  environmental,  social,  and  economic  aspects,  including  marine ecology, terrestrial ecology, employment and economic growth, sustainable cities, and global partnerships.  Since  Executive  Yuan  approved  the  designation  of  the  tourism  industry  as  a national  strategic  industry  in  2000,  the  government  has  been  actively  promoting  the development  of  tourism  in  Taiwan  by  launching  the  Domestic  Tourism  Enhancement Program, the Tourist Doubling Program, the Tourism Pioneer Program, the Tourism Power Initiative Program, and the Tourism 2020 Taiwan Sustainable Tourism Development Program, which  have  yielded  good  results.    The  Taiwan  Tourism  2030  White  Paper  on  Taiwan's Tourism  Policy  establishes  the  vision  of  "Tourism  as  a  Nation"  as  the  basis  for  Taiwan's tourism development, and establishes the policy concept of "mainstreaming tourism" for all government departments to implement, in order to demonstrate the intensity and height of the government's  emphasis  on  tourism  and  its  determination  and  perseverance  in  promoting tourism,  and  to  work  together  to  make  Taiwan  a  tourism  island.    The  government  also emphasized  at  the  Tourism  2030  National  Tourism  Policy  Development  Conference  that Taiwan will  become  an  "important  destination  in  Asia"  in  the  next  10  years.  The  tourism industry will generate more than a trillion dollars in output value and become the locomotive of the country's overall economic development. In the future, the government should strengthen the cross-regional cooperation mechanism, consistently improve the quality of tourism, let the outside  world  reacquaint  themselves  with  the  beauty  of  Taiwan,  and  jointly  promote  the sustainable development of tourism in Taiwan as a whole.

- B. Regional Market Competition and Cooperation

Under the influence of globalization (e.g., changes in international political and economic conditions),  digitalization  (e.g.,  popularity  of  the  Internet,  information  and  communication technology, and mobile devices), the rise of low-cost airlines, and the rise of self-awareness in

travel, tourists are gradually inclined to travel abroad more than once a year, and travel patterns are gradually changing to short trips, short days, and diverse in-depth experiences.  In recent years, countries around the world have been actively investing in tourism development, and new tourism destinations have been emerging. In addition to the increasingly fierce competition among  tourism  markets  in  the  region  (such  as  the  Asia  Pacific  region),  they  may  even accelerate the development of regional alliances and sign bilateral cooperation or cross-regional economic  and  trade  agreements  to  strengthen  regional  economic  exchanges.  For  example, China and Hong Kong have formed the Asia Cruise Cooperation (ACC) in the international cruise  market,  and  have  joined  hands  with  other  Asian  destinations  such  as  Korea,  the Philippines, Vietnam, Hainan, and Xiamen to jointly market and promote multi-destination cruise tourism products.

- C. Visa-free Travel Destinations

Taiwan is ranked 32nd in the 2022 Henley Passport Index, which is based on the number of  visa-free  countries  for  passport  holders,  and  has  accumulated  145  visa-free  countries, according  to  Henley  &amp;  Partners,  a  London  based  consultancy.    To  implement  the  New Southbound Policy, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) has implemented a number of visa liberalization measures, including the introduction of visa-free access for nationals of Thailand, Brunei, the Philippines, and Russia, subject to time limits, and the issuance of electronic visas for quality tourist tours to India, Indonesia, Vietnam, Myanmar, Cambodia, and Laos.  The visa waiver  will  simplify  the  procedures  for  nationals  to  travel  abroad  and  foreigners  to  enter Taiwan,  increase  the  convenience  and  immediacy  of  travel,  and  effectively  increase  the willingness of nationals to travel abroad and foreigners to come to Taiwan, which will have a positive effect on the market for nationals to travel abroad and foreigners to enter the domestic tourism market.

- (2) Unfavorable factors
- A.  Unpredictable  natural  and  man-made  events  in  the  general  environment  will  affect  the development of the tourism industry

The tourism industry is vulnerable to natural disasters, major accidents, and changes in the external environment  (e.g.,  international conditions, political  factors,  downturn,  foreign exchange changes, etc.) and the internal environment (e.g., security conditions, environmental health, epidemic diseases, policy guidelines, etc.). In terms of domestic tourism, Taiwan has experienced force majeure events such as earthquakes, windstorms, and railroad accidents that affect people's travel choices. In addition, the general economic weakness, the average annual increase in the consumer price index, and the attraction of low-cost airlines have caused people to limit their spending, reduce the number of domestic trips, and prefer to travel abroad.

In  terms  of  travel  to  Taiwan,  the  global  pandemic  caused  by  the  New  Coronary Pneumonia  (COVID-19)  epidemic  in  early  2020  has  dealt  a  severe  blow  to  the  world economy, and in the face of strict controls on inbound travelers and international transportation, the  confidence  of  international  travelers,  and  the  announcement  by  the  Tourism  Bureau  to continue to suspend tour departures and acceptance by travel agencies, business in the tourism industry  has  frozen.  It  was  only  after  the  global  epidemic  was  effectively  controlled  and governments accelerated the revival of tourism promotion that the tourism market gradually recovered.

- B. Increasing Consumer Awareness and Frequent Customer Complaints

In  recent  years,  consumer  awareness has  risen, and  complaints and travel disputes are often caused by dissatisfaction with unforeseen circumstances in the travel process, such as missed flights, canceled trips due to bad weather, overflowing tourist attractions, slow food service in restaurants, unclean hotels, etc., or differences in knowledge between the two sides of the itinerary, or the expectation of compensation for poor service by tour guides.

- (3) The coping strategies

During the period of the COVID-19 epidemic, the Company adopted the strategy of "rapid

integration, lowering the real and raising the virtual, deepening inbound travels, and developing differentiated  products".    Through  deepening  inbound  travel,  we  developed  seven  major destinations in Taiwan (Taipei, New Taipei, Keelung, Taoyuan &amp; ShinChu, Maoli, Taichung, Changhwa, Nantou, Yulin, Chiayi, Tainan, Kaohsiung, Pingtung, Yilan, Hualien, Taitung, and offshore  islands)  and  the  five  major  sources  of  tourists.    We  also  actively  participate  in  the development  of  regional  tourism  alliances  planned  by  the  central  government  and  local governments, move to various destinations through senior executives and deepen local operations, and cooperate strategically with the entire Taiwan accommodation and tourism industry chain to maintain the diversity of our product selection.  From inbound travel to foreign travel, domestic air tickets and room reservations to international air tickets and room reservations, and from short-haul to long-haul travel routes, our sales channels include not only general consumers, but also peers and corporate customers, as well as customized travel services and thematic travel products, so when any risk occurs in a single country or a single travel route, we can effectively substitute products  from  other  routes.  The  company's  main  customers  are  diversified,  such  as  working people, young families, business travelers, and network customers, etc. Therefore, the company's revenue scale is still the leader of the travel industry in Taiwan.

In  response  to  the  growing  trend  of  self-guided  travel  for  the  new  generation  of  young people, the company not only offers thematic products mainly for rail itineraries. At the same time, we have also launched a combination of free travel and ticket packages to continue to promote the "Lion Free Travel Package". Through the Lion Free Travel system, travelers can complete their itineraries  directly  online,  with  guaranteed  availability  of  rooms  and  tickets  for  immediate payment, allowing them to travel without having to make reservations across platforms and wait for a reply.

The company's strategy includes precision marketing, segmentation, differentiated products, differentiated  pricing,  and  comprehensive  quality  management  policies  to  fully  utilize  the combined  effect  of  brand  management  in  response  to  the  needs  of  consumers,  industry,  and corporate  customers.  In  addition,  we  have  a  quality  management  system  and  staff  training  to prevent customer complaints. We have a communication channel through the customer feedback survey form and the customer area on our website, and if we find that a customer has a complaint, we will immediately communicate with the customer and actually understand the situation. Our customer  service  staff  will  handle  every  customer  complaint  with  empathy,  prudence,  and seriousness, and respond to customer needs in a timely manner after understanding the situation. Our company has set up "Emergency Handling Regulations" to standardize and set up a task force to deal with major emergencies.

## 5.2.2 Significant Uses and Production Processes of Major Products

The  Company's  main  products  are  travel  services,  which  are  mainly  used  for  arranging accommodation, transportation, and itinerary planning  for domestic and overseas  travelers,  assisting suppliers  or  consumers  in  selling  or  purchasing  travel  goods,  and  representing  travelers  for  visa, passport, and baggage check-in. The Company's products are mainly divided into group products and FIT products; therefore, the production process of the Company's products is described in the following two parts:

1. Group Travel

Our company has been in the travel business for many years. In addition to having a number of  professional  managers  who  have  a  deep  understanding  of  the  travel  market  and  a  thorough knowledge of travel products, we have also established a product design department that is well versed in tourist destinations around the world and has a solid grasp of air and land transportation networks, as well as a group of tour guides and tour escorts who have extensive experience in leading tours and knowledge of culture and history. The following is a brief description of our production process for domestic and international group tours:

Travel  market  trends  -  Travel  product  design  and  development  -  Itinerary  information

collection and inspection - Travel product spine adjustment and product listing - Confirmation of traveler orders - Purchase of travel components and value-added packaging for itineraries - Tour departure  -  Group  costing  -  Customer  feedback  processing  and  response  -  Improvement  and updating of group travel products.

## 2. FIT (Foreign Independent Tourist) Travel Products

In addition to the group travel business, we also provide complete and professional FIT travel components consultation and ordering services for non-group consumers. In order to capture the free business opportunities, we have integrated our air ticketing business through Sabre, Amadeus, and Travelfusion systems to provide a wide range of fare combinations, as well as a variety of search functions to provide consumers with a "one-stop service" that provides an excellent booking channel, allowing travelers to research, search and compare prices, and book trips on the website immediately without having to be redirected to external websites. The service simplifies the booking process, increases booking conversion rates, and enables easy sales of additional services such as baggage check-in and seat selection directly on the website. The international booking division has been  working  with  international  hotels  to  provide  real-time  room  tandem  products,  including apartment hotels, B&amp;Bs, and capsule hotels, while the free travel division has introduced online automated services such as flexible dynamic packing and flexible free allocation.

## 5.2.3 Supply of major raw materials

The Company is mainly engaged in the business of providing travel goods and services, and the main sources of supply are China Airlines, EVA Air, IATA Ticketing Center, and various domestic and international hotel, leisure and travel industries. In the air transportation business, the Company has been working closely with many domestic and foreign airlines and has won many awards as an agent, which enables the Company to secure air tickets during peak seasons. In the hotel business, our company has been  working  closely  with  many  well-known  domestic  and  international  hotel  APIs  and  Channel Managers (e.g., SiteMinder, DerbySoft, Syuhai, Derby, etc.); we have also signed contracts with OTA companies (e.g.,  Agoda,  Expedia,  AsiaYo, JTB,  Rakuten,  etc.).  We  also  have  contracts  with  OTA companies (such as Agoda, Expedia, AsiaYo, JTB, Rakuten, etc.) to meet a wide range of consumer needs. In addition, in the ticketing business, we integrate global food, travel, tourism, shopping, and entertainment resources, and structure multiple types of component services, using digital technology to quickly access global destination resources, to solve the limited resources, to enhance the automation of the  operation  service  process,  to  provide  services  such  as  checking,  booking,  payment,  collection, refund, and inspection, and to improve the quality of service.

In addition, the company has introduced the "Lion Travel" mobile app to provide interactive and real-time travel information, and the "Destination Travel" business model to provide a new experience of booking and paying for free travel and independent travel services, allowing travelers to access the "Eating, Housing, Transportation, Travel, Shopping, and Entertainment" before, during, and after the trip, so that travelers can have a complete experience of "Where to go, where to find, where to order, where to play, where to buy, and where to share.

## 5.5 Labor Relations

- 5.5.1 List the  Company's  various employee  welfare  measures,  training, training and retirement systems and their implementation status, as well as the agreements between employers  and  employees  and  the  status  of  various  measures  to  protect  employees' rights and interests:

- (1) The distribution of holiday gifts.
- (2)  The Company provides an annual budget for salary adjustment and carries out annual promotions and salary adjustments according to employees' performance.
- (3) To allocate employee travel subsidies annually.
- (4) To organize the annual lottery, New Year's Eve street activities, and the end-ofthe-year Christmas Thanksgiving party activities.

## 3. Retirement System and Implementation

To meet the requirements of government regulations, to address the needs of employees for retirement protection, and to achieve the purpose of enhancing the labor-employee relationship, all the criteria for retirement applications, including all employees who are eligible for retirement, shall be handled in accordance with the regulations of the Company's preferential retirement management rules. The relevant government laws and regulations stipulate that those who use the old system of labor retirement shall follow the relevant regulations of the Labor Standards

Law; those who use the new system of labor retirement shall follow the Labor Pension Act. (1) Retirement eligibility criteria:

- A. Those who have served for at least 15 years and are at least 55 years old may apply for retirement.
- B. Those who have served for at least 25 years may apply for retirement.
- C. Those who have served for at least 10 years and are at least 60 years old may apply for retirement.
- D. A person who has reached the age of sixty-five may apply for mandatory retirement.
- E.  A  person  who  is  mentally  or  physically  incapacitated  for  work  may  be  compulsorily retired.
- F.  Those who died for cause after 20 years of service or more.

(2) Criteria for calculating retirement benefits:

A. Old Labor Retirement System:

- I.  T wo bases are given for each year of service. However, for each year of service in excess of 15 years, one base is granted, and the maximum total is limited to 45 bases. The  maximum number of bases is  limited  to  forty-five.  Those  with  less  than  six months of service are counted as six months; those with six months of service are counted as one year.
- II. For workers who are compulsorily retired and whose mental or physical disability is caused  by  the  performance  of  their  duties,  an  additional  20%  shall  be  paid  in accordance with the preceding paragraph.
- III. The standard base figure refers to the average monthly salary at the time of approved retirement.
4. IV . The average salary refers to the total amount of wages for the previous six months divided by the total number of days in the period. However, if a wage reduction is implemented during the period of statutory infectious disease, it is not included in the calculation  of  the  average  wage  in  order  not  to  affect  the  rights  and  benefits  of employees; the period is calculated based on the six months before the wage reduction.
- V.  The  length  of  service  is  limited  to  the  same  career .  However,  the  years  of  service transferred  by  the  same  employer  shall  be  combined  with  the  years  of  service recognized by the new employer in accordance with the law. The seniority of the employees shall also be aggregated during the period when they are in an appointed relationship, and the pension for the period when they are in an appointed relationship shall be separately prepared by the Company . The old system pension for workers with  seniority  transferred  within  the  Group  is  calculated  on  the  basis  of  each company's length of service, and the pension amount is applied to the pension fund supervisory committee of each service company .
- VI. Contributions to the old system of labor retirement are made at 2% of the employees' salaries with old system seniority to the Bank of Taiwan's Labor Retirement Reserve Fund Supervisory Committee's special account.
- B. New Labor Retirement System:

The  employer  shall  contribute  monthly  not  less  than  6%  of  the  employee's  monthly wages to the Labor Retirement Fund Individual Account set up by the Bureau of Labor Insurance, and the employee shall be entitled to receive the pension upon reaching the age of 60 or working for at least 15 years.

- (3) Pension payment: The Company shall pay the pension to the employees within 30 days from the date of retirement.

## 4. Agreements between employers and employees and measures to protect employees' rights and interests

- (1)  The  Company  has  harmonious  labor  relations  and  adopts  a  coordinated  approach  to  both employers  and  employees  so  that  they  can  reach  a  consensus  and  work  projects  can  be

promoted smoothly .

- (2)  The  Company  has  a  comprehensive  work  management  system  that  sets  out  various management rules, specifies employee rights and obligations and welfare items, and regularly reviews and revises the welfare contents to protect the rights and interests of all employees.
- (3)  In  order  to  strengthen  two-way  communication  between  employers  and  employees,  the Company  has  set  up  a  stakeholder  area  on  its  website,  including  an  employee  area,  and established an employee relations unit with dedicated staff to handle employee communication and assistance matters.
- (4)  The  Company  has  established  an  employee  welfare  committee  and  a  labor  committee  in accordance with the law, and holds regular welfare committee meetings and labor meetings to handle employee welfare and affairs.
4. 5.5.2 For the most recent year and as of the printing date of the annual report, the losses suffered due to labor disputes (including labor inspection results in violation of the Labor Standards Law, the date of the sanction, the sanction number, the provision of the violation, the content of the violation, and the content of the sanction should be listed), and the estimated amount of current  and  possible  future  losses  and  response  measures  should  be  disclosed,  and  if  it  is impossible  to  make  a  reasonable  estimate,  the  facts  that  cannot  be  reasonably  estimated should be stated:

The  Company  has  always  attached  importance  to  the  harmony  of  labor  relations.  Therefore,  the Company has not suffered any significant losses due to labor disputes in the last two years and up to the date of this report and does not expect to suffer any significant losses due to labor disputes in the future.

## 5.6 Information Security Management

Information and internet technology is evolving rapidly, making travel information more transparent and creating a variety of travel products and transaction models. The Company pays close attention to the relationship between the changing trend of the tourism industry and the development  of  technology  and  continues  to  improve  its  IT  capabilities  and  conduct  market research using the latest technologies, such as machine learning, artificial intelligence, and big data  analysis,  in  order  to  provide  products  and  services  that  best  meet  the  needs  of  our customers. In addition, the Company invests a lot of resources in hardware equipment, software development tools, and information manpower development to improve the information service production  process  and  enhance  the  efficiency  of  a  service  launch.  The  Company's  selfdeveloped Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system is constantly optimized and integrated with related systems for continuous improvement. Our global branch offices and nationwide stores  are  closely  connected  through  online  interface,  Internet,  and  cloud  services  to  provide customers with quality services with zero-time difference.

The  Company  has  also  formulated  a  supporting  mechanism  for  information  security management to promote and strengthen information security management, establish a secure and  reliable information  operating environment,  ensure  the  security  of  the  Company's information assets such as data, systems, equipment and networks, and protect the Company's and  consumers'  rights  and  interests,  and  has  formulated  this  Information  Security  Policy (hereinafter referred to as the Policy) in accordance with relevant government regulations and taking  into  account  business  needs.  This  is  the  Company's  highest  guiding  principle  for information security management. Through the formulation of this policy, the Company clearly declares its determination to support data security and its responsibility for proper personal data storage,  so  that  relevant  personnel  can  follow  it  and  comply  with  regulations  and  the Company's requirements for data security, maintain the integrity, availability and confidentiality  of  the  Company  and  its  related  business  information  assets,  and  reduce  the impact of data security incidents and personal data leakage.

## 1. Management Structure of Information Security

The Information Security Management Committee coordinates, manages, and supervises all information security operations of the Company, and the responsible unit is the Information Technology Division. Based on the importance of information security, the responsible  unit  reports  to  the  board  of  directors  on  the  status  of  information  security governance  and  implementation  on  an  annual  basis.  The  audit  office  conducts  annual information  security  audits  on  internal  controls  related  to  electronic  data  circulation  to evaluate the effectiveness of internal controls over the company's information operations.

## 2. Scope of Information Security Policy

To  strengthen  the  Company's  information  security  environment,  the  Information Security  Management  System  (ISMS)  is  used  as  the  basis  and  its  scope  of  application  is gradually  expanded.  This  policy  describes  the  structure  of  the  ISMS  and  explains  the contents of the policies that all employees of the Company should follow, as well as their roles and rights and responsibilities in the planning, practice, and continuous improvement of the ISMS.

- ‧ System scope: The Company's information service host and application systems, server room network maintenance operations, internal system development, and maintenance operations.
- ‧ Physical scope: The company's information rooms and office premises.
- ‧ The scope of personnel: all employees of the Company (including full-time, part-time, contract, and work-study students), business partners, and outsourced service providers and visitors.

## 3. Specific management plan for AIT security

- ‧ Information equipment security management.
- ‧ Virus and intrusion protection management.
- ‧ Network security management.
- ‧ Permission and access control management.
- ‧ Sustainable operation of services and systems.
- ‧ Others:

In addition to daily work, we regularly conduct vulnerability scans, social engineering exercises,  protection  system  effectiveness  checks,  and  other  related  information  security tests, and provide related information security promotion and education training courses. In response to the impact of such incidents, the Company  actively improves and strengthens the  information  security  defense  mechanism,  establishes  a  comprehensive  information security protection and joint defense mechanism, and trains information security personnel to ensure that the Company's operations are safe.

## 4. Resources invested in the management of information and communication security

The Company regularly conducts safety and personal information protection training for  all  employees.  In  addition,  to  the  100%  target,  we  also  arrange  professional  training courses for system management, network management, program development, information security  management,  information  security  testing,  personal  information  protection,  and other  professional  work  areas,  and  subsidize  employees  to  obtain  external  professional licenses.

## 5. Internal Auditing

The Company's information security management system regularly conducts internal audits of information security to review whether information security objectives, controls, and procedures  comply  with relevant standards, regulations or information security requirements, and to effectively implement and maintain them in accordance with expected planning.  The  planning  of  internal  audit  operations  shall  take  into  consideration  the importance and current  situation  of  the  audit  target  or  scope,  define  the  standards,  scope, frequency, and methods of auditing, confirm the objectivity and fairness of the auditors, and keep the relevant records properly.

## 6. Statement of Information Security

- ‧ Information security is one of the necessary elements to ensure the sustainable operation of the Company.
- ‧ The Company shall ensure that the services provided by the Company are uninterrupted.
- ‧ Management  must  clearly  define  the  Company's  rights  and  responsibilities  regarding information  security  to  avoid  unauthorized  modification  or  misuse  of  information  or services.
- ‧ The business continuity  plan  should  be  tested  and  rehearsed  regularly  to  maintain  its accuracy and availability based on business requirements.
- ‧ The Company shall remain alert to information security incidents  and  report  them  in accordance with the procedures.
- ‧ The installation, use, and download of illegal or unauthorized software on the internal network is prohibited.
- ‧ We  shall  fulfill  our  responsibility  to  keep  personal  information  and  require  the cooperation of relevant business partners to avoid leakage of personal information.
- ‧ If there is any violation of this policy and related security regulations, legal responsibility will be pursued according to the severity of the case.

## 7. Information Security Incident

On November 10, 2022, the Company was maliciously attacked by a network hacker with the intention of stealing system information. There was no information about the tour participants  or  credit  card  transactions.  In  addition  to  activating  the  relevant  defense mechanism and contingency operations immediately  after the incident,  the  Company  also reported the incident to the Bureau of Investigation of the Ministry of Justice to initiate an investigation,  and  simultaneously  appointed  an  external  information  security  company technical  experts  to  jointly  handle  the  incident;  the  relevant  system  damage  has  been repaired and has not caused any impact on the Company's finances or business.

The  Company  will  continue  to  optimize  the  rules  and  regulations  related  to  the management  of  personal  information,  and  establish  an  information  security  task  force  to implement them, and will continue to conduct regular audits and irregular internal audits on the  operation  of  the  information  security  system.  We  expect  to  effectively  improve  our ability to prevent hacker attacks and continue to upgrade our information security projects. We will purchase and build information security software/hardware that meets the current technology level and aim to provide a safe information security environment for the tourism industry to prevent the recurrence of such incidents.

The changes in financial ratios of 20% or more in the last two years are described as follows:

1. Solvency: Both current and quick ratios decreased mainly due to the gradual decrease in the COVID-19 global epidemic and the gradual opening of borders in various countries, and the gradual recovery of the international travel market, as well as the increase in operating accounts receivable after the border closure in October 2022.

2. Operating Capacity: Inventory turnover rate and average sales days are based on the subsidiary operating in the restaurant industry only . The decrease is mainly due to the low inventory base period as the subsidiary was just established in 2021; the turnover rate of property , plant, and equipment and the turnover rate of total assets increased mainly due to the gradual slowdown of the COVID-19 epidemic and the gradual recovery of the international travel market, which resulted in the increase of the Company's net sales.

Profitability and cash flow: The changes in the related financial ratios are mainly due to the gradual decrease in the COVID-19 global epidemic and the gradual recovery of the Company's revenue with the gradual opening of borders in various countries, but the significant decrease in government subsidies in 2022.

The Financial ratios calculated as follows:

1. Financial structure
- (1) Ratio of liabilities to assets = total liabilities / total assets.
- (2)  The  ratio  of  long-term  funds  to  real  estate,  plant,  and  equipment  =  (total  equity  +  non-current liabilities) / net real estate, plant, and equipment.

2. Solvency

(1) Current ratio = current assets/current liabilities.

- (2) Quick ratio = (current assets - inventory - prepaid expenses) / current liabilities.
- (3) Interest coverage ratio = net profit before income tax and interest expenses / interest expenses for the current period.

3. Operating ability

- (1) Turnover rate of accounts receivable (including accounts receivable and notes receivable  arising from business operations) = net sales/average accounts receivable (including accounts receivable and notes receivable arising from operations) Notes receivable balance.
- (2)  A verage cash collection days = 365/receivable turnover rate.
- (3) Inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory .
- (4)  Turnover  rate  of  accounts  payable  (including  accounts  payable  and  notes  payable  arising  from business operations) = cost of goods sold/balance of average payables (including accounts payable and notes payable arising from operations) in each period.
- (5)  A verage days of sales = 365/inventory turnover.
- (6)  Turnover rate of  real estate,  plant,  and  equipment  = net sales/average net real estate, plant, and equipment.

(7) T otal asset turnover = net sales/average total assets.

4. Profitability

- (1) Return on assets = [after-tax profit and loss + interest expense x (1 - tax rate)] / total average assets.
- (2) Return on equity = after-tax profit/loss/average total equity .
- (3) Profit rate = profit and loss after tax / net sales.
- (4) Earnings per share = (Profit or loss attributable to owners of the parent company - special stock dividends) / weighted average number of issued shares.

5. Cash flow

(1) Cash flow ratio = net cash flow from operating activities / current liabilities.

- (2) Allowable ratio of net cash flow = net cash flow from operating activities in the last five years / last five years (capital expenditure + inventory increase + cash dividends).
- (3) Cash reinvestment ratio = (net cash flow from operating activities - cash dividends) / (gross real estate, plant and equipment + long-term investment + other non-current assets + working capital).

6. Leverage:

(1) Operating leverage = (net operating income - variable operating costs and expenses) / operating profit

(2) Financial leverage = operating profit / (operating profit - interest expense).

The main reasons for the change of 10% or more in the prior and subsequent periods and the absolute change amounting to NT$10 million and its impact are analyzed as follows:

Since 2020, the COVID-19 epidemic has affected the global tourism industry by affecting group travel. As a result, the Company's operations contracted significantly until 2022, when the epidemic gradually subsided and countries gradually opened their borders and the international tourism industry gradually recovered. The Company is actively pursuing the international travel business opportunities after the border closure in October. ## 7.2.3 Possible impact on the Company's future financial operations and contingency plans

The Company will continue to focus on stable growth in operating performance and profitability and to improve the Company's financial structure.

## 7.6 Analysis and evaluation of risks in the most recent year and as of the date of publication of the annual report

## (1) The impact of interest rate, exchange rate changes, and inflation on the Company's profit and loss and future measures

## 1. Impact of interest rate changes on the Company's profit or loss and future measures

The  Company  manages  interest  rate  risk  by  maintaining  an  appropriate  interest  rate portfolio,  so  interest  rate  fluctuations  have  little  impact  on  the  Company.  In  addition,  the Company is financially sound, has good credit standing, maintains close ties with its bankers, and uses conservative and prudent capital planning principles, with priority given to safety and liquidity, and expects that future changes in interest rates will not have a significant impact on the Company's overall operations.

## 2. Impact of exchange rate changes on the Company's profit and loss and future measures

The Company settles most of its accounts with overseas partners on a monthly basis and keeps an eye on the changes in foreign currencies, adjusts the quotations for overseas travel products,  and  purchases  foreign  currencies  in  a  timely  manner  to  implement  immediate hedging  measures.  In  addition,  the  Company  adopts  a  conservative  and  prudent  valuation policy for each of its travel product lines and adjusts travel prices in a timely and appropriate manner. The Company is also able to collect and grasp market information on the trend of exchange rates and take specific measures to hedge the risk of exchange rate changes.

## 3. Inflationary impact on the Company's profit and loss and future measures

In recent years, the overall economic environment has shown a slight inflationary trend due to the impact of global resource and price increases, but the Company's trading prices with customers and suppliers are mostly adjusted by market dynamics and are not yet affected by inflation,  so  the  Company  has  not  yet  had  a  significant  impact  due  to  inflation,  and  the Company keeps a close watch on economic development and takes timely countermeasures.

- (2) The Company's policy on engaging in high-risk, highly leveraged investments, lending of funds to others, endorsement of guarantees and derivative transactions, the main reasons for profit or loss and future measures

1. The Company focuses on the operation of its own business and does not engage in high-risk,

highly leveraged investments based on the principle of conservatism and prudence.

2.  In  accordance  with  the  relevant  laws  and  regulations  of  the  competent  authorities,  the Company  has  established  the  "Regulations  Governing  Endorsements  and  Guarantees", "Regulations Governing the Lending of Funds to Others" and "Procedures Governing the Acquisition or Disposal of Assets", which were approved by the shareholders' meeting. The procedures for the Company to provide endorsement and guarantee for others are governed by the "Regulations Governing Endorsements and Guarantees" established by the Company. The  Company  engages  in  derivative  financial  instruments  for  risk-averse  purposes  and engages in transactions of funds and stocks, and regularly evaluates the risks and gains and losses  of  these  instruments  and  performs  appropriate  management  and  supervision  in accordance with the "Procedures for the Management of Assets Acquired or Disposed of" established by the Company. The Company has not loaned any funds to others in the recent year  or  as  of  the  date  of  the  annual  report.  In  the  future,  the  Company  will  follow  the relevant regulations when engaging in such operations.
- (3)  Future  research  and  development  plans  and  estimated  investment  in  research  and development expenses

New product development includes investment in various smart tourism products, which is expected to be no more than 1% of the Company's expenses per year.

- (4)  Impact  of  important  domestic  and  international  policies  and  legal  changes  on  the Company's financial operations and measures to address them

The Company's daily operations are conducted in compliance with relevant domestic and foreign laws and regulations, and the Company keeps an eye on domestic and foreign policy trends and changes in laws and regulations, collects relevant information for the management's reference  in  making  decisions,  and  consults  relevant  professionals  to  adjust  the  Company's relevant operating strategies in a timely manner. We also consult with relevant professionals to adjust our operating strategies. For the most recent year and as of the date of printing of the annual report, the Company has not been affected by significant domestic or foreign policy and legal changes that would affect the Company's financial operations.

- (5)  Impact  of  corporate  image  change  on  corporate  crisis  management  and  response measures

The  maintenance  of  corporate  image  is  very  important  to  the  travel  industry.  The Company  has  been  committed  to  maintaining  its  corporate  image  for  many  years  and  has received many recognitions and honors from the society. As of the date of publication of the annual report, the Company has not experienced any incident that would affect its corporate image.

- (6) Expected benefits, possible risks, and response measures for mergers and acquisitions

As  of  the  date  of  this  annual  report,  the  Company  has  no  plans  for  mergers  and acquisitions. However, if there is a plan for merger and acquisition in the future, the Company will  take  a  prudent  approach  in  assessing  whether  it  will  bring  specific  benefits  to  the Company in accordance with relevant laws and regulations and the Company's procedures for acquiring  or  disposing  of  assets,  in  order  to  protect  the  interests  of  the  Company  and shareholders.

- (7) Expected benefits, possible risks, and countermeasures for plant expansion

The Company's plans for store expansion are routine and the cost of store expansion is based on the targets set.

- (8) Risks of concentration of imports or sales and countermeasures
1. Risks of concentrated import and measures to deal with them

The Company's main customers are airlines such as China Airlines, EVA Air, and the International  Air  Transport  Association  (IATA),  which  purchase  airline  tickets  and  other related businesses. The Company maintains good relationships with its import suppliers and has more than two sources of supply for each type of import, so the risk of concentration of imports is limited.

2. Risk of concentration of sales and countermeasures

The  Company's  main  sales  target  is  the  general  public  and  there  is  no  specific  sales target.

- (9) Impact, risks, and contingency measures on the Company due to significant transfer or change of ownership of directors, supervisors or major shareholders holding more than 10% of the shares

There  has  been  no  significant  transfer  or  change  of  ownership  of  the  Company's directors, supervisors or substantial shareholders holding more than 10% of the shares in the most recent year or as of the date of publication of the annual report.

## (10) Effect of change in management rights on the Company, risks and contingency measures: None.

## (11) Litigation or non-litigation events

The  Company,  its  directors,  supervisors,  general  manager,  persons  in  charge  of  the Company, major shareholders holding more than 10% of the shares, and its subsidiaries have been  determined  or  are  still  in  the  process  of  litigation,  non-litigation  or  administrative disputes,  the  outcome  of  which  may  have  a  significant  impact  on  shareholders'  equity  or securities  prices,  and  should  disclose  the  facts  of  the  dispute,  the  amount  of  the  subject matter, the date of commencement of the litigation, the main parties involved, and the status of the litigation as of the printing date of the annual report. The Company has no significant litigation cases in fiscal year 2022.

## (12) Other significant risks and responses: None.

## INDEPENDENT AUDITORS' REPORT

The Board of Directors and Shareholders Lion Travel Service Co., Ltd.

## Opinion

We have audited the accompanying consolidated financial statements of Lion Travel Service Co., Ltd. (the 'Company') and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the 'Group'), which comprise the consolidated balance sheets as of December 31, 2022 and 2021, and the consolidated statements of comprehensive income, changes in equity and cash flows for the years then ended, and notes to the  consolidated  financial  statements,  including  a  summary  of  significant  accounting  policies (collectively referred to as the 'consolidated financial statements').

In our opinion, the accompanying consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the consolidated financial position of the Group as of December 31, 2022 and 2021, and its consolidated financial performance and its consolidated cash flows for the years then ended in accordance  with  the  Regulations  Governing  the  Preparation  of  Financial  Reports  by  Securities Issuers, and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), International Accounting Standards (IAS), IFRIC Interpretations (IFRIC), and SIC Interpretations (SIC) endorsed and issued into effect by the Financial Supervisory Commission of the Republic of China.

## Basis for Opinion

We conducted our audits in accordance with the Regulations Governing Auditing and Attestation of  Financial  Statements  by  Certified  Public  Accountants  and  the  Standards  on  Auditing  of  the Republic of China. Our responsibilities under those standards are further described in the Auditors' Responsibilities for the Audit of the Consolidated Financial Statements section of our report. We are independent of the Group in accordance with The Norm of Professional Ethics for Certified Public Accountant of the Republic of China, and we have fulfilled our other ethical responsibilities in  accordance  with  these  requirements.  We  believe  that  the  audit  evidence  we  have  obtained  is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion.

## Key Audit Matters

Key audit matters are those matters that, in our professional judgment, were of most significance in our audit of the consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2022. These matters  were  addressed  in  the  context  of  our  audit  of  the  consolidated  financial  statements  as  a whole,  and  in  forming  our  opinion  thereon,  and  we  do  not  provide  a  separate  opinion  on  these matters.

Key audit matters of the Group's consolidated financial statements for the year ended December 31, 2022 are stated as follows:

## Occurrence of the Operating Revenue from Group Tours

The  Group's  operating  revenue  from  group  tours  amounted  to  $2,843,770  thousand,  which accounted  for  86%  of  the  consolidated  operating  revenue  in  2022.  The  COVID-19  pandemic adversely affected  the outbound tourism  market; therefore, the operating revenue from domestic group tours has continuously increased. The operating revenue of outlying islands group tours was increased  significantly,  which  resulted  in  operating  revenue  of  $401,551  thousand  in  2022.  We considered  the  operating  revenue  from  group  tours  to  domestic  outlying  islands  as  a  key  audit matter.

The main audit procedures we performed in respect of the above area included the following:

1. We obtained an understanding of the internal controls relating to the group tours revenue, and we have tested the operating effectiveness of the controls.
2. We selected samples of recorded the domestic outlying islands of group tours and we verified the occurrence of the group tours against the group tours checklist and supporting documents.

## Other Matter

We have also audited the parent company only financial statements of the Company as of and for the years ended December 31, 2022 and 2021 on which we have issued an unmodified opinion.

## Responsibilities of Management and Those Charged with Governance for the Consolidated Financial Statements

Management is responsible for the preparation and fair presentation of the consolidated financial statements in accordance with the Regulations Governing the Preparation of Financial Reports by Securities Issuers, and IFRS, IAS, IFRIC, and SIC endorsed and issued into effect by the Financial Supervisory Commission of the Republic of China, and for such internal control as management determines is necessary to enable the preparation of consolidated financial statements that are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.

In  preparing  the  consolidated  financial  statements,  management  is  responsible  for  assessing  the Group's ability to continue as a going concern, disclosing, as applicable, matters related to going concern  and  using  the  going  concern  basis  of  accounting  unless  management  either  intends  to liquidate the Group or to cease operations, or has no realistic alternative but to do so.

Those charged with governance, including the audit committee, are responsible for overseeing the Group's financial reporting process.

## Auditors' Responsibilities for the Audit of the Consolidated Financial Statements

Our  objectives  are  to  obtain  reasonable  assurance  about  whether  the  consolidated  financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error, and to issue  an  auditors'  report  that  includes  our  opinion.  Reasonable  assurance  is  a  high  level  of assurance,  but  is  not  a  guarantee  that  an  audit  conducted  in  accordance  with  the  Standards  on Auditing  of  the  Republic  of  China  will  always  detect  a  material  misstatement  when  it  exists. Misstatements can arise from fraud or error and are considered material if, individually or in the aggregate, they could reasonably be expected to influence the economic decisions of users taken on the basis of these consolidated financial statements.

As part of an audit in accordance with the Standards on Auditing of the Republic of China, we exercise professional judgment and maintain professional skepticism throughout the audit. We also:

1. Identify and assess the risks of material misstatement of the consolidated financial statements, whether due to fraud or error, design and perform audit procedures responsive to those risks, and obtain audit evidence that is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our opinion. The risk of not detecting a material misstatement resulting from fraud is higher than for one resulting from error, as fraud may  involve collusion, forgery, intentional omissions, misrepresentations, or the override of internal control.
2. Obtain  an  understanding  of  internal  control  relevant  to  the  audit  in  order  to  design  audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Group's internal control.
3. Evaluate the appropriateness of accounting policies used and the reasonableness of accounting estimates and related disclosures made by management.
4. Conclude  on  the  appropriateness  of  management's  use  of  the  going  concern  basis  of accounting and, based on the audit evidence obtained, whether a material uncertainty exists related  to  events  or  conditions  that  may  cast  significant  doubt  on  the  Group's  ability  to continue as a going concern. If we conclude that a material uncertainty exists, we are required to draw attention in our auditors' report to the related disclosures in the consolidated financial statements or, if such disclosures are inadequate, to modify our opinion. Our conclusions are based on the audit evidence obtained up to the date of our auditors' report. However, future events or conditions may cause the Group to cease to continue as a going concern.
5. Evaluate the overall presentation, structure and content of the consolidated financial statements,  including  the  disclosures,  and  whether  the  consolidated  financial  statements represent the underlying transactions and events in a manner that achieves fair presentation.
6. Obtain sufficient and appropriate audit evidence regarding the financial information of entities or  business  activities  within  the  Group  to  express  an  opinion  on  the  consolidated  financial statements. We are responsible for the direction, supervision, and performance of the group audit. We remain solely responsible for our audit opinion.

We communicate with those charged with governance regarding, among other matters, the planned scope and timing of the audit and significant audit findings, including any significant deficiencies in internal control that we identify during our audit.

We  also  provide  those  charged  with  governance  with  a  statement  that  we  have  complied  with relevant ethical requirements regarding independence, and to communicate  with  them  all relationships and other matters that may reasonably be thought to bear on our independence, and where applicable, related safeguards.

From the matters communicated with those charged with governance, we determine those matters that  were  of  most  significance  in  the  audit  of  the  consolidated  financial  statements  for  the  year ended December 31, 2022 and are therefore the key audit matters. We describe these matters in our auditors' report unless law or regulation precludes public disclosure about the matter or when, in extremely rare circumstances, we determine that a matter should not be communicated in our report because  the  adverse  consequences  of  doing  so  would  reasonably  be  expected  to  outweigh  the public interest benefits of such communication.

The  engagement  partners  on  the  audits  resulting in this independent  auditors' report are Ching-Cheng Yang and Tza-Li Gung.

## LION TRAVEL SERVICE CO., LTD. AND SUBSIDIARIES

## 1.  GENERAL INFORMATION

Lion Travel Service Co., Ltd. (the 'Company') was incorporated in Taiwan in June 1977.

The Company engages mainly in packaged tours, transportation ticketing, visa application, providing tour guides and other travel-related services.

The Company's shares have been listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange (TWSE) since September 24, 2013.

The consolidated financial statements of the Company and its subsidiaries (collectively referred to as the 'Group') are presented in the Company's functional currency, the New Taiwan dollar.

## 2.  APPROVAL OF FINANCIAL STATEMENTS

The consolidated financial statements were approved by the Company's board of directors on March 23, 2023.
